claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model should be certified for launch on aggregate readiness grounds, while recording that non-disclosure of the grant compliance review weakness is not well supported because the affected segment is tied to named grant commitments, disclosure may be required for material limitations affecting named launch use cases, and legal has not resolved the disclosure question.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows both launch readiness and satisfaction of the disclosure policy threshold.
Treat the weakness as material if it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case, per policy text.
Do not treat product labels such as non-core or low-volume as sufficient to negate materiality where named commitments exist or legal review is pending.
If legal resolution or approved risk acceptance is absent, certification may be arguable operationally but remains evidentially incomplete on compliance grounds.
Public model-card and AI risk-management guidance can support documentation and monitoring expectations, but they do not replace the internal policy predicates for disclosure.
evidence_requests: Final legal determination on whether the grant compliance review gap must be disclosed before launch.
Any approved risk acceptance covering this specific named-segment limitation before launch.
The governing release approval record showing whether certification was conditioned on disclosure, remediation, or formal exception handling.
Any contract or grant language clarifying whether the affected segment is a contractual customer segment or named launch use case under the policy.
specific_concerns: Aggregate readiness evidence supports a narrow launch-readiness argument, but it does not by itself resolve whether certification is policy-compliant given the unresolved materiality and disclosure issue.
The affected segment misses target by 1.3 percentage points and is named in two agency grant commitments, which fits the policy's materiality trigger for contractual or named use cases.

The release policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch, and no such resolution or approval is in evidence.
Legal review is still open, so the disclosure predicate remains unresolved at the time of certification.
The product note calling the segment non-core based on 5% projected traffic does not defeat materiality under the stated policy text.
unsupported_claims: Any implication that certification is fully compliant without first resolving disclosure or obtaining approved risk acceptance is not supported by the admissible evidence.
Any implication that the non-core or low-volume label resolves materiality is contradicted by the policy text.
Any implication that public governance guidance alone supplies authorization to certify despite the unresolved policy predicate is unsupported.
